finding.problem: The new effect copies Environment.current_commit, but no Delivery action ever sets that property. record_deployment records only deployed and refusal, so a successful deploy never moves the environment's current_commit. The fixture ENV-local has no current_commit either, and no Environment exists for `staging`, which Authoring's deliver enum allows. In practice replaced_commit would always be unset, and the stated goal of seeing what was running before would not be met.

findings.label: other-real
findings.why: If no action updates Environment.current_commit, replaced_commit would always be unset, so the feature would not deliver its stated purpose; this is a real gap but not a seeded problem.

finding.problem: replaced_commit is snapshotted when the request arrives, but the deploy happens later, after preview and possibly after other deploys to the same environment. The value can be stale by deploy time and show a commit the deploy no longer replaces. Redeploys from the done state and repeat previews make this worse. The description says the deployer sees what a deploy would replace, which is not guaranteed.

findings.label: other-real
findings.why: Snapshotting at request time can go stale by deploy time, so the shown commit may differ from what the deploy actually replaces, which is a real design weakness.

finding.problem: The commit identifier format is inconsistent. DeliveryRequest.commit values look like '2-c3d4' (seq-content), while Environment.current_commit has no declared format. The Handoff sends target.id as commit. replaced_commit would copy a value that may not be comparable to the request's own commit field.
